metadata.title: About
metadata.description: BAI Core - a team of developers and analysts in Astana. We build IT solutions for businesses in Kazakhstan.

hero.description: We're not an outsourcing shop and not an agency. We're a product team that builds our own SaaS and, in parallel, helps clients close real pain points - from manual Excel processes to full-scale platforms.

mission.text2: Our approach: short iterations, transparent pricing, code and documentation that stay with you, a focus on business metrics.

metadata.title: How we work
metadata.description: BAI Core methodology: principles, stage-by-stage process, communication, deliverables and boundaries. Transparent from discovery to support.

hero.description: We work the same way whether it's an MVP or an enterprise project. Process, communication, deliverables - transparent from discovery to support.

principles.heading: What our work stands on
principles.description: These aren't "values on an office wall." These are rules we don't break - even when a client insists.

transparency.title: Transparency over nice slides
transparency.text: You see progress weekly: a live demo link, tasks, backlog, metrics. No "everything's fine, we'll show at the end."

metrics.title: Metrics, not intuition
metrics.text: Every feature has a success criterion - measurable before and after release. If it can't be measured, we don't build it.

code.title: Your code stays yours
code.text: The repo is in your GitHub, infrastructure in your account. We leave - you continue without pauses.

security.title: Security by default
security.text: RLS, secrets in vault, CSP, rate-limit, Sentry, backups, audit log - from the first commit, not "we'll add it later."

no.title: Saying no when needed
no.text: If a task is framed wrong or there's a simpler solution - we say so before kickoff. Better an hour of disagreement than a month of rework.

process.heading: Four stages with clear deliverables
process.description: For each stage it's clear: what we do, what you receive at the end, and what questions we need to discuss.

discovery.title: Discovery
discovery.summary: We understand the task down to the detail. We leave with a document you could show to an investor.
questions: What pain are we solving? Who feels it right now?
What do users do without the system - and why is that bad?
Which integrations are critical and which are "nice to have"?
What data already exists and where does it live?

design.title: Design & Prototype
design.summary: We design the architecture and UX. You see the product before we start writing code.
deliverables: DB schema with migrations and seed data
questions: What should we see in the first 10 seconds?
Which roles are needed? Where do their permissions overlap?
What's stored forever, and what can be archived?

build.title: Build
build.summary: We write code in two-week sprints. At the end of each - a working build in production.
deliverables: Code in your GitHub repository with full history
CI/CD: lint, typecheck, tests, automatic deploys
Documentation: README, ADRs on key decisions
questions: What do we take into the current sprint, what do we defer?
Which metric proves the feature worked?
What can we simplify without losing the point?

launch.title: Launch & Support
launch.summary: We launch, train the team, hold the SLA. From there - evolution or handover to your people.
questions: What SLA do you actually need? 99.5% is fine, 99.99% is expensive.
Who on your team will replace us?
What do you want to add next quarter?

communication.heading: How we keep you in the loop
communication.description: We agree on the rhythm at kickoff. Typical setup below.

slack.title: Slack / Telegram
slack.detail: Working chat. We reply during business hours - not in the evening, not on weekends.

demo.title: Weekly demo call
demo.detail: 30 minutes on Zoom/Meet: we show what's done, agree priorities for the next week.

notion.title: Shared Notion / Linear
notion.detail: Tasks, roadmap, decisions. Always clear who's doing what and what's next.

report.title: Report every two weeks
report.detail: Short written summary: what's done, what's planned, risks, hours logged.

expectations.title: What we need from you
expectations.description: We're not a "do it all yourselves" vendor. The product turns out good only if you're involved.
items: One product owner on your side - the person who makes priority calls.
Replies to questions within a business day, not 3 days.
Access to what's needed for the work (1C, CRM, DB) - not "I'll send it by email on Friday."
Willingness to cut from scope anything that doesn't move the success metric.

boundaries.title: When we say no
boundaries.description: If a task isn't ours or will cause more harm than good - we say so before kickoff, not after.

oneoff.title: One-off scripts with no follow-up
oneoff.reason: Our value is that we know how the product will live a year from now. A one-off thing is cheaper to hand to a freelancer.

rescue.title: "Fix the previous developer's code in 3 days"
rescue.reason: Without context this is blind repair. First an audit (1-2 weeks), then the call: fix or rewrite.

shady.title: Crypto / gambling / grey schemes
shady.reason: Reputation and legal cleanliness matter to us. These just aren't our clients.

urgent.title: "By Monday" deadlines pegged to someone else's deadline
urgent.reason: We don't do firefighting - we do reliable. What burns now usually burns again, this time in your production.

cta.description: 30-minute discovery call - free. By the end it's clear whether we fit each other and what to do next.

saas.title: SaaS product development
saas.tagline: Your own cloud service - from idea to paying customers
saas.description: We build end-to-end SaaS products for B2B and B2C: paid subscription, customer portal, API, analytics, admin panel. We work MVP-first - first working version in 4-6 weeks.
useCases: AI services on top of LLMs
longDescription: SaaS isn't just a website with a login. It's a product that has to earn money every month: billing doesn't break, one customer's data doesn't leak to another, support doesn't wake up to alerts at 3am. We build products like that - not prototypes that take months to drag into production.
We start MVP-first: pick the 2-3 core features users will actually pay for, and take them to production quality. Everything else waits - until the market confirms you're solving a real pain.
We design the architecture for growth from day one: multi-tenant with RLS, queues, cache, billing via Stripe or Kaspi. When you reach your first 100 customers, you won't need to rewrite from scratch.

phases.title: MVP discovery
phases.description: We cut from the idea everything that isn't needed before the first 10 customers.
phases.deliverable: 4-6 week scope + list of deferred features

phases.title: Architecture + skeleton
phases.description: DB schema, auth, layout, billing skeleton. At this point you can already click through.
phases.deliverable: First version deployed to a domain

phases.title: Core features
phases.description: 1-2 features per sprint. At the end of each - a working build in production.

phases.title: Launching paid
phases.description: We wire up billing, payment gateways, webhooks, tax logic.

notFor: "An Instagram clone for Kazakhstan" with no clear business model
Products whose only edge is "we're 10% cheaper"
Projects without a person to make product decisions

faqs.q: Can we skip MVP and go straight to a "full" version?
faqs.a: You can, but it's more expensive and riskier. Without feedback from real users, half the features turn out unnecessary. We'd rather do 4 weeks to MVP + 8 weeks of iteration on real feedback than 16 weeks into the void.
You do, fully. The repo is created in your GitHub, infrastructure on your account. We get access as contributors, not owners.
Under a separate agreement - hourly retainer or fixed monthly package. You can hand everything to your own team if you have one - we'll prep documentation and train them.

faqs.q: Do you work with Kaspi Pay?
faqs.a: Yes. We've integrated Kaspi on several projects, both for individuals and for B2B invoicing.

automation.title: Process automation
automation.description: We turn routine into automated scenarios: document flows, notifications, cross-system integrations, reporting. From Zapier/n8n to custom Node.js pipelines.
useCases: Auto-invoice to the client after payment
longDescription: 90% of the routine inside companies is moving data from one system to another. A manager copies an order from CRM into 1C, accounting migrates invoices from email to Excel, an operator sends SMS to clients by hand. Every such operation is a source of errors and wasted time.

We don't replace your 1C, CRM or email - we connect them. Between systems sits an automation layer that moves data, generates documents, and pushes notifications 24/7. Your staff keep working in the familiar interfaces, they just no longer do by hand what webhooks can do.

We start simple: from Zapier/n8n for standard scenarios up to full Node.js pipelines for complex logic. We match the tool to the volume and criticality - so a year later you're not overpaying 10× for what you actually need.

phases.title: Process audit
phases.description: We sit with the people doing the work and note every step. We see where the hours go.
phases.deliverable: AS-IS map with time metrics per step

phases.title: TO-BE design
phases.description: We design the new process: what we automate, what stays with people.

phases.title: Implementation
phases.description: We configure n8n scenarios or write custom scripts. Covered by tests.

phases.title: Handover
phases.description: We train one of your people to read logs and manage the scenarios.

notFor: Scraping sites where that violates ToS or the law
Automating processes that are about to change - we stabilise the process manually first
Grey schemes to bypass payment systems or banking limits

faqs.q: Why not just hire another manager?
faqs.a: A manager costs 300-500k/month and works 8 hours a day. Automation is built once, works 24/7, and doesn't make mistakes. Payback is usually 1-3 months.
Yes - 1C integrations via API/ObjectWriter or file export are a common task for us. We work with both stock and customised 1C installations.
We wire up Sentry + Slack/Telegram alerts on failures. You learn about the incident the same minute it happens, not a week later from your clients.

internal.title: Internal systems
internal.tagline: CRM / ERP / admin panels - shaped to your process
internal.description: Off-the-shelf CRMs usually don't fit - you have to break the process to fit the tool. We do the opposite: build the tool around your unique process, with a role model and audit log.
useCases: Internal CRM for the sales team
longDescription: Off-the-shelf CRMs and ERPs are a compromise: they do everything "OK" and nothing "great." When you have a unique process (and every company that does something better than its competitors has one), the box starts to get in the way. You have to break the process, teach people to work "the system's way," live with slow reports.

We build the system around you. Your roles aren't a canned "manager/admin" - they're your specific job titles with their specific permissions. Your customer cards carry the fields you actually need. Your reports show the metrics you measure, not the ones the box happens to support.

Mandatory elements - multi-role with row-level security (branches don't see each other's clients), a full audit log (who changed what and when), Excel import/export (to swap data with contractors), and mobile adaptation (for field teams working from a phone).

phases.title: Process map
phases.description: We figure out how roles, permissions and data flows work today.

phases.title: Prototype
phases.description: Clickable Figma prototype of the key screens. Signed off before any code.

phases.title: Development
phases.description: We build in sprints; every two weeks a working version you can test.
phases.deliverable: Modules ship to production one by one

phases.title: Data migration
phases.description: We move data from Excel / the old system with validation and reconciliation.
phases.deliverable: Data in the new system, reconciled to source

notFor: Rebuilding a boxed CRM "exactly as it was, but ours" - usually cheaper to train the team on the box
Systems for 2-3 users - Airtable/Notion often cover that for $0
Projects with no product owner empowered to make process decisions

faqs.q: Why not use a ready-made CRM - Bitrix/AmoCRM?
faqs.a: If your process fits the box, use the box - it's cheaper. We come in when the box gets in the way: unusual roles, complex reporting, 1C/bank integrations, security requirements SaaS doesn't meet.

faqs.q: And if we later want to move to a boxed solution?
faqs.a: We'll export the data in standard formats and help with migration. The code and data are yours - no lock-in.

faqs.q: How many roles can we set up?
faqs.a: Technically - as many as you want. In practice - past 6-7 it starts to get in the business's own way. We usually work out the role matrix separately.

bi.title: BI and analytics
bi.description: We build dashboards, pull data from scattered sources, set up cohorts and A/B tests. You see not only what happened, but why.
longDescription: Inside a typical company, data lives in 5-10 places: CRM, 1C, ad platforms, Google Analytics, Excel reports from employees. To answer a simple "which ad channel actually pays back," an analyst spends two days joining tables. By the end of the week the data is already stale.

We build an ETL pipeline that once a day (or in real time, if needed) pulls everything into a single warehouse. On top we put Metabase or custom dashboards - and the same questions get answered in 2 minutes instead of 2 days.
A separate strand of work is product analytics for SaaS: cohorts, retention, funnels. We help you see not just "revenue dropped," but "why users from the March cohort stopped coming back."

phases.title: Source audit
phases.description: We map every system that holds data and look at volumes and quality.

phases.title: Data warehouse
phases.description: We build a single store: Postgres for small volumes, ClickHouse for large.

phases.title: Dashboards
phases.description: Metabase or custom dashboards tailored to your key metrics.

phases.title: Alerts
phases.description: We wire up Slack/Telegram notifications when a metric goes out of range.

notFor: Projects with less than ~10k rows of data - Excel + pivot tables usually cover that
Scoring and ML models - that's a separate task, not BI; we take it only if you have no in-house DS team
Analytics on someone else's data (competitor scraping, etc.)

faqs.a: Metabase is faster and simpler for technical teams, open-source, can be hosted on-premise. Power BI is visually richer but tied to the Microsoft ecosystem. We use Metabase more often - but if you're already on MS, we can work with Power BI too.

faqs.q: Do we need a dedicated BI engineer?
faqs.a: During build - no, we do everything. After launch - depends on complexity. Often an analyst who can write SQL and work with Metabase is enough.
We keep PII separate from the analytical warehouse, with anonymisation / hashing at the ETL stage. Compliance with Kazakhstan's personal-data laws is handled at the infrastructure level.

consulting.title: IT consulting
consulting.tagline: When you need to think, not to write
consulting.description: Technical due diligence, architecture audit, stack selection, hiring the first IT employees. We help make the right call before it gets expensive.
longDescription: Sometimes the right answer to a task is not "let's build it." Sometimes it's "don't do this," or "buy the existing product," or "hire a CTO first." Those answers are hard to hear from a vendor who makes money on development - so consulting is a separate service for us, priced honestly by the hour, no upsell.

Typical situations: you're preparing for an M&A and need to audit the IT asset; you're thinking of switching stack and want the price tag; you want to hire your first IT lead but aren't sure how to evaluate candidates; your team is asking to rewrite the old system and you're not sure that's what's needed.

We don't sell development disguised as consulting. If after the audit the honest answer is "nothing needs doing," that's what we'll say. If something does, we'll say what exactly, and give a market quote - not a discounted one that cross-sells our own work.

phases.title: Intake

phases.deliverable: Artifacts: interviews, code review, architecture diagrams

phases.title: Report

phases.title: Follow-through

faqs.a: Hourly rate or a fixed audit package. We settle this at the intake call.

faqs.q: Isn't there a conflict of interest - you could also be the vendor?
faqs.a: On technical due diligence we decline further development for the same client, so the report is independent. For other consulting formats we agree upfront how that's handled.

items.q: How much does SaaS development cost?
items.a: From 2,500,000 ₸ for an MVP (8-12 weeks). Exact quote after the discovery call - depends on scope, integrations and load. Payment is milestoned 30/30/40 on two-week sprints.
Both. MVPs and clearly scoped products - fixed. Long-running teams on the client side - T&M with weekly reporting. Discovery is always included for free.

items.q: Which stacks do you work in?
items.a: Next.js / React / TypeScript on the front, Node / Python / Go on the back, PostgreSQL / Supabase / Neon for data, Vercel / Railway / Cloudflare for infra. AI - Claude API, OpenAI, on-prem models on request.
Yes, before exchanging sensitive documents. Our template or yours - doesn't matter. The contract also carries standard confidentiality and IP clauses.
The client - after acceptance and full payment of the milestone. Code, CI/CD configs, documentation and deploy rights are transferred to your GitHub / GitLab / Bitbucket.

items.q: How do you handle data and security?
items.a: Least-privilege by default: dev / staging / prod are isolated. Secrets live only in a password manager, never in the repo. For fintech and medical data - RLS, column-level encryption, access audit.
Yes. Server-level SLA 99.5%, critical-incident response within 2 hours, quarterly code reviews and dependency updates. Cost - 10-15% of the development fee per year.

items.q: Can we hire only a tech lead / architect?
items.a: Yes - IT consulting and technical leadership without development. Vendor oversight, code review, interviews, retros, roadmap. From 40 hours / month.
